# Jubilees Chapter 37 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Ge'ez MS; cf. 4QJub (Hebrew fragments) | **Section:** Esau breaks his oath; the war between Jacob and Esau begins

---

**37:1** And in the first year of the first week of the forty-sixth jubilee, Esau returned against Jacob his brother to make war with him.

**37:2** For he had heard that Jacob had gathered together much wealth at Hebron — silver, gold, cattle, camels, and horses. And Esau gathered together his four thousand warriors and went to the land of Canaan against Jacob.

**37:3** And Jacob heard that Esau was coming against him with four thousand men, and he was afraid. And Jacob built a tower and made a wall of stone around it.

**37:4** And Jacob sent a message to his brother Esau: "I have seen thy face as one sees the face of God, and thou hast been gracious to me. Why dost thou come against me with swords and shields to kill me and my household?"

**37:5** And Esau sent to him: "Though I swore peace with thee before thy mother Rebekah, I have not forgotten the days of thy deception and the wrong thou didst to me."

**37:6** And Jacob said to his sons and to his household: "Arm yourselves and come against Esau, for he is coming against us with a great host."

**37:7** And Jacob's sons armed themselves — Reuben, Simeon, Levi, Judah, Dan, Naphtali, Gad, Asher, Issachar, Zebulun, and Joseph. And there were four hundred with them.

**37:8** And they went out against Esau and his four thousand men. And there was a great battle in the mountains of Hebron.

**37:9** And Judah slew Adoran, and Dan slew his king, and Naphtali slew his enemy, and Gad slew his adversary.

**37:10** And Reuben killed the king of the Aramaeans who was with Esau. And the battle was fierce all that day.

**37:11** And at the end of the day Esau fled with his men, and they went back to Seir. And Jacob and his sons pursued them to the borders of Seir.

**37:12** And Esau made peace again with Jacob and they swore a second time, saying: "Let there be peace between us from this day until the end of our lives."

**37:13** And the sons of Jacob returned from the pursuit and went back to Hebron.

**37:14** And Jacob and his sons rested after the battle, and they rejoiced greatly, for Esau had been driven back.

**37:15** And in that day Isaac died, being a hundred and eighty years old, in the forty-sixth jubilee, in the fifth week, in the first year.

**37:16** And Jacob buried his father at Mamre in the cave of Machpelah with Abraham and Sarah his grandparents.

---

*EMET notes: The war between Jacob and Esau (chs.37-38) is unique to Jubilees and the Testament of Judah tradition; it has no parallel in Genesis. In Jubilees, Esau breaks his oath and attacks Jacob, which is presented as the fulfillment of Isaac's warning about Mastema (ch.36:6). The sons of Jacob function as warriors here, not merely shepherds.*
